name: The Winstons
hook: A Washington soul band whose drummer's six-second solo on a B-side became the most famous drum break in the world.

blurb.age7: A soul band. Their drummer played a very short drum solo that other musicians have copied thousands of times.
blurb.age13: The Winstons were a soul band from Washington, D.C. Their 1969 hit 'Color Him Father' won a Grammy for its writer, the saxophonist Richard Spencer. On the other side of the single was 'Amen, Brother', where the drummer Gregory Coleman plays a drum solo about six seconds long. Hip-hop producers sampled it, then in the 1990s British jungle and drum and bass producers chopped it up and sped it up until it was the sound of a whole genre. It's called the Amen break. Spencer never got paid for any of it. In 2015 two British DJs raised about 24,000 pounds for him online.
blurb.adult: The Amen break is the defining case of a sample outgrowing its source. Spencer, who held the copyright, received no royalties from its thousands of uses, and the 2015 fundraiser was a goodwill gesture, not a settlement. Coleman, who played it, is reported to have died in 2006 without recognition. The break's life in jungle and drum and bass is a major cross-lineage story that this map doesn't carry yet (BACKLOG).
